No, they are not the same scenario. They are entirely different:

| | **Frosthaven Scenario 61** | **Gloomhaven 2e Scenario 61** |
|---|---|---|
| **Title** | *Life and Death* | *Dangerous Grove* |
| **Monsters** | Deep Terror, Harrower Infester | Cave Bear, Forest Imp, Hound |
| **Objectives** | Escort ally (Moonshard) | None listed |
| **Unlocks** | See section 67.1 | Scenario 62 |
| **Flow group** | Puzzle book | Personal quests |

**Frosthaven Scenario 61 – "Life and Death"** is a complexity-2 escort mission set in the Copperneck Mountains. You must keep an NPC ally named Moonshard alive while killing all enemies; if she dies, the scenario is lost. Characters also each add two cards to their attack modifier deck as a scenario effect.

**Gloomhaven 2e Scenario 61 – "Dangerous Grove"** is a personal-quest-linked scenario featuring Cave Bears, Forest Imps, and Hounds. The checked-in data for this one does not include full raw text, page number, or complexity.

Here are the two sections, drawn from verified tool results.

---

## Frosthaven — Section 67.1 ("Life and Death")

*Source: Frosthaven Section Book, p. 67 — linked to Scenario 61*

> Your ears fill with the sound of your own breathing: heavy, stinging, rib-pulling breaths. Your legs are full of acid, ready to seize, but you push through the pain and exhaustion, struggling to keep up with Moonshard…

The full conclusion scene plays out around a campfire outside the cave. You meet an Orchid elder named **Terra**, who explains that she has foreseen this moment for 200 years and introduces you to a quartz-bodied Savvas lineage called **the Shattersong** — uniquely attuned to the thoughts of a being called **the Harbinger**. Terra explains that the Harbinger is bound deep within the earth, corrupting and plotting its escape, and that your group has a "slim chance" of stopping it. Crain excitedly mentions needing **star iron** to reinforce the seals; Moonshard dismisses it as myth.

**Rewards:**
- Unlock class box.

**Section Links:**
- Add **section 140.3** to the calendar in **one week**.

---

## Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) — Section 67.1 ("The Last Stand")

*Source: Gloomhaven 2e Section Data — linked to Scenario 55*

This is a **structured encounter section** (Room 6) with no narrative text in the record. It sets up the following monsters by player count:

| Monster | 2P | 3P | 4P |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black Imp | Elite | Elite | Normal |
| Chaos Demon | Normal | Normal | Elite |
| Deep Terror | Normal | Elite | Elite |
| Harrower Infester | — | Normal | Elite |

*(One Black Imp and one Chaos Demon are present at all player counts as base spawns.)*

---

## Are They the Same Section?

**No, they are completely different.** The section number "67.1" is shared only by coincidence of numbering:

- **Frosthaven 67.1** is a narrative conclusion scene from Scenario 61 ("Life and Death"), introducing Terra and the Shattersong and advancing the Harbinger storyline.
- **Gloomhaven 2e 67.1** is a monster-placement encounter section for Scenario 55 ("The Last Stand"), with no narrative content — only room setup data.

The two games maintain entirely separate section books with independent numbering, so the same section number refers to unrelated content in each game.

Here are the two sections, exactly as retrieved.

---

**Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) — Section 67.1: "The Last Stand"**
*(Source: gloomhavensecretariat:sections/67-1, parent scenario 55)*

This is a structured room-setup section. It lists the monsters deployed in Room 6, scaled by player count:

- *Black Imp* (normal / elite by count)
- *Chaos Demon* (normal / elite by count)
- *Deep Terror* (normal / elite by count)
- *Harrower Infester* (normal / elite by count)

---

**Frosthaven — Section 67.1: "Life and Death" conclusion**
*(Source: Section Book 62–81, p. 67, linked to scenario 61)*

This is a narrative conclusion section — a lengthy story passage featuring the characters Moonshard, Crain, Terra, and the Shattersong, culminating in exposition about the Harbinger. Rewards: unlock a class box. Section link: add section 140.3 to the calendar in one week.

---

**Can either section serve as evidence for the other game?**

**No.** The two sections share only a number. Their content is entirely unrelated — one is a monster-deployment table for a Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) scenario, the other is a Frosthaven narrative conclusion for a completely different scenario. They are separate products with separate section books, separate scenario structures, and separate storylines. Numbering coincidences carry no rules or narrative weight across the two games.
